units.scope: content of binding corporate rules
units.proposition: A controller or processor adopting binding corporate rules is obliged to specify the structure and contact details of the group and of each of its members in those rules.

units.addressee: controller or processor adopting binding corporate rules
units.action: specify the data transfers or sets of transfers, including the categories of personal data, the type of processing and its purposes, the type of data subjects affected, and the identification of the third country or countries
units.scope: content of binding corporate rules
units.proposition: A controller or processor adopting binding corporate rules is obliged to specify the relevant data transfers or sets of transfers, including categories of personal data, types and purposes of processing, types of data subjects affected, and the identification of the third country or countries.

units.ru_label: No recognition of third-country data-transfer orders without agreement
units.action: recognise a judgment or administrative decision requiring a controller or processor to transfer or disclose personal data
units.scope: Any judgment of a court or tribunal and any decision of an administrative authority of a third country that requires a controller or processor to transfer or disclose personal data, in any manner within the Union
units.condition: The judgment or decision is not based on an international agreement, in force, between the requesting third country and the Union or a Member State
units.exception: Without prejudice to other grounds for transfer pursuant to this Chapter
units.proposition: Do not recognise, in any manner, any judgment or decision of a third-country court, tribunal, or administrative authority that requires a controller or processor to transfer or disclose personal data if it is not based on an international agreement in force between the requesting third country and the Union or a Member State, without prejudice to other grounds for transfer pursuant to this Chapter.

units.action: take appropriate steps to develop international cooperation mechanisms to facilitate the effective enforcement of legislation for the protection of personal data
units.scope: in relation to third countries and international organisations
units.proposition: The European Commission is obligated, in relation to third countries and international organisations, to take appropriate steps to develop international cooperation mechanisms to facilitate the effective enforcement of legislation for the protection of personal data.

units.action: take appropriate steps to develop international cooperation mechanisms to facilitate the effective enforcement of legislation for the protection of personal data
units.scope: in relation to third countries and international organisations
units.proposition: Supervisory authorities are obligated, in relation to third countries and international organisations, to take appropriate steps to develop international cooperation mechanisms to facilitate the effective enforcement of legislation for the protection of personal data.

units.action: provide for one or more independent public authorities to be responsible for monitoring the application of this Regulation
units.scope: independent public authorities responsible for monitoring application of the GDPR
units.proposition: Each Member State is obliged to provide for one or more independent public authorities that are responsible for monitoring the application of the GDPR.

units.action: contribute to the consistent application of this Regulation
units.scope: throughout the Union
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority is obliged to contribute to the consistent application of the GDPR throughout the Union.

units.action: cooperate with each other and the Commission
units.scope: in accordance with Chapter VII
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority is obliged to cooperate with the other supervisory authorities and the Commission in accordance with Chapter VII.

units.action: act with complete independence
units.scope: when performing its tasks and exercising its powers
units.condition: in accordance with this Regulation
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority is obliged to act with complete independence when performing its tasks and exercising its powers in accordance with this Regulation.

units.addressee: member or members of each supervisory authority
units.action: remain free from external influence
units.scope: in the performance of their tasks and the exercise of their powers; external influence may be direct or indirect
units.condition: in accordance with this Regulation
units.proposition: The member or members of each supervisory authority are obliged to remain free from external influence, whether direct or indirect, in the performance of their tasks and the exercise of their powers in accordance with this Regulation.

units.addressee: member or members of each supervisory authority
units.action: seek instructions from anybody
units.scope: in the performance of their tasks and the exercise of their powers
units.condition: in accordance with this Regulation
units.proposition: The member or members of each supervisory authority are prohibited from seeking instructions from anybody in the performance of their tasks and the exercise of their powers in accordance with this Regulation.

units.action: provide for each member of their supervisory authorities to be appointed by means of a transparent procedure by one of the following authorities: the parliament, the government, the head of State, or an independent body entrusted with the appointment under Member State law
units.scope: members of the supervisory authorities of the Member State
units.proposition: Member States are obliged to ensure that each member of their supervisory authorities is appointed through a transparent procedure by the parliament, the government, the head of State, or an independent body entrusted with the appointment under Member State law.

units.addressee: each member of a supervisory authority
units.action: have the qualifications, experience and skills required to perform duties and exercise powers, in particular in the area of the protection of personal data
units.scope: members of a supervisory authority
units.proposition: Each member of a supervisory authority is obliged to have the qualifications, experience and skills required to perform the duties and exercise the powers, in particular in the area of the protection of personal data.

units.ru_label: End of duties on expiry, resignation or retirement
units.addressee: the competent authority under Member State law
units.action: end a member’s duties
units.scope: members of a supervisory authority
units.condition: in the event of expiry of the term of office, resignation or compulsory retirement, in accordance with the law of the Member State concerned
units.proposition: The competent authority under Member State law is obliged to end a member’s duties upon expiry of the term of office, resignation or compulsory retirement, in accordance with the law of the Member State concerned.

units.action: provide by law for the establishment of each supervisory authority
units.scope: each supervisory authority within the Member State
units.proposition: Each Member State shall provide by law for the establishment of each supervisory authority.

units.action: provide by law for the qualifications and eligibility conditions required to be appointed as member of each supervisory authority
units.scope: qualifications and eligibility conditions for appointment as member of each supervisory authority
units.proposition: Each Member State shall provide by law for the qualifications and eligibility conditions required to be appointed as member of each supervisory authority.

units.action: provide by law for a duration of office for the member or members of each supervisory authority of no less than four years
units.scope: duration of the term of office of the member or members of each supervisory authority
units.exception: Except for the first appointment after 24 May 2016, part of which may be set for a shorter period where necessary to protect the independence of the supervisory authority by means of a staggered appointment procedure.
units.proposition: Each Member State shall provide by law for a duration of the term of the member or members of each supervisory authority of no less than four years, subject to the stated exception for the first appointment after 24 May 2016.

units.action: be competent for the performance of the tasks assigned to it
units.scope: on the territory of its own Member State
units.condition: in accordance with this Regulation
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority has the power to perform the tasks assigned to it, in accordance with this Regulation, on the territory of its own Member State.

units.addressee: supervisory authority of the main or single establishment of the controller or processor
units.action: act as lead supervisory authority
units.scope: for cross-border processing carried out by the relevant controller or processor
units.condition: in accordance with the procedure provided in Article 60
units.exception: without prejudice to Article 55
units.proposition: The supervisory authority of the main or single establishment of the controller or processor has the power to act as the lead supervisory authority for cross-border processing by that controller or processor, subject to the procedure in Article 60 and without prejudice to Article 55.

units.action: handle a complaint lodged with it
units.scope: a case under this Regulation
units.condition: the subject matter relates only to an establishment in its Member State or substantially affects data subjects only in its Member State
units.exception: by derogation from paragraph 1
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority has the power to handle a complaint lodged with it if the subject matter relates only to an establishment in its Member State or substantially affects data subjects only in its Member State, by derogation from paragraph 1.

units.addressee: supervisory authority handling a case under paragraph 2
units.action: inform the lead supervisory authority about the matter
units.scope: the case referred to in paragraph 2
units.condition: in the cases referred to in paragraph 2
units.proposition: A supervisory authority handling a case under paragraph 2 must inform the lead supervisory authority about the matter without delay.

units.action: monitor the application of this Regulation
units.scope: on its territory
units.condition: without prejudice to other tasks set out under this Regulation
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority shall, on its territory and without prejudice to other tasks set out under this Regulation, monitor the application of this Regulation.

units.action: promote public awareness and understanding of the risks, rules, safeguards and rights in relation to processing
units.scope: on its territory
units.condition: without prejudice to other tasks set out under this Regulation
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority shall, on its territory and without prejudice to other tasks set out under this Regulation, promote public awareness and understanding of the risks, rules, safeguards and rights in relation to processing.

units.action: give specific attention to activities addressed specifically to children in its public awareness and understanding activities
units.scope: on its territory
units.condition: without prejudice to other tasks set out under this Regulation
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority shall, on its territory and without prejudice to other tasks set out under this Regulation, give specific attention to activities addressed specifically to children in its public awareness and understanding activities.

units.action: order the controller, the processor, and, where applicable, their representative to provide any information the supervisory authority requires for the performance of its tasks
units.scope: investigative powers
units.condition: Where applicable regarding the representative; the information is required for the performance of the supervisory authority's tasks
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority has the power to order the controller, the processor, and, where applicable, their representative to provide any information the supervisory authority requires for the performance of its tasks.

units.action: carry out investigations in the form of data protection audits
units.scope: investigative powers
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority has the power to carry out investigations in the form of data protection audits.

units.action: notify the controller or the processor of an alleged infringement of this Regulation
units.scope: investigative powers
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority has the power to notify the controller or the processor of an alleged infringement of this Regulation.

units.action: draw up an annual report on its activities
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority is obliged to draw up an annual report on its activities.

units.ru_label: Optional inclusion of infringement and measures list
units.action: include in the annual report a list of types of infringement notified and types of measures taken in accordance with Article 58(2)
units.scope: content of the annual activity report
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority is permitted to include in its annual report a list of types of infringement notified and types of measures taken in accordance with Article 58(2).

units.action: transmit the annual activity report to designated recipients
units.scope: the national parliament, the government, and other authorities as designated by Member State law
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority is obliged to transmit its annual activity report to the national parliament, the government and other authorities as designated by Member State law.

units.action: cooperate with the other supervisory authorities concerned to reach consensus
units.scope: in accordance with Article 60
units.proposition: The lead supervisory authority shall cooperate with the other supervisory authorities concerned in accordance with Article 60 in an endeavour to reach consensus.

units.action: exchange all relevant information with the other supervisory authorities concerned
units.proposition: The lead supervisory authority shall exchange all relevant information with the other supervisory authorities concerned.

units.ru_label: LSA power to request mutual assistance
units.action: request other supervisory authorities concerned to provide mutual assistance
units.scope: pursuant to Article 61
units.proposition: The lead supervisory authority may at any time request other supervisory authorities concerned to provide mutual assistance pursuant to Article 61.

units.action: provide each other with relevant information and mutual assistance
units.scope: to implement and apply the GDPR in a consistent manner
units.proposition: Supervisory authorities are obligated to provide each other with relevant information and mutual assistance to implement and apply the GDPR in a consistent manner.

units.action: put in place measures for effective cooperation with one another
units.proposition: Supervisory authorities are obligated to put in place measures for effective cooperation with one another.

units.action: ensure that mutual assistance covers information requests and supervisory measures, including requests to carry out prior authorisations and consultations, inspections and investigations
units.scope: scope of mutual assistance between supervisory authorities
units.proposition: Supervisory authorities are obligated to ensure that mutual assistance covers information requests and supervisory measures, including requests to carry out prior authorisations and consultations, inspections and investigations.

units.action: conduct joint operations, including joint investigations and joint enforcement measures, involving members or staff of supervisory authorities of other Member States
units.scope: joint operations across Member States
units.condition: where appropriate
units.proposition: Supervisory authorities shall, where appropriate, conduct joint operations, including joint investigations and joint enforcement measures, involving members or staff of supervisory authorities of other Member States.

units.addressee: supervisory authority of each Member State concerned
units.action: participate in joint operations
units.scope: Member States where the controller or processor has establishments or where data subjects are likely to be substantially affected
units.condition: the controller or processor has establishments in several Member States, or a significant number of data subjects in more than one Member State are likely to be substantially affected by processing operations
units.proposition: A supervisory authority of each concerned Member State has the right to participate in joint operations when the controller or processor has establishments in several Member States or when a significant number of data subjects in more than one Member State are likely to be substantially affected by processing operations.

units.addressee: supervisory authority competent pursuant to Article 56(1) or (4)
units.action: invite the supervisory authority of each concerned Member State to take part in the joint operations
units.scope: joint operations under Article 62(2)
units.condition: the controller or processor has establishments in several Member States, or a significant number of data subjects in more than one Member State are likely to be substantially affected by processing operations
units.consequence: If it does not comply within one month, other supervisory authorities may adopt provisional measures on their territory under Article 55; in that case, the urgent need to act under Article 66(1) is presumed and an opinion or urgent binding decision from the Board under Article 66(2) is required.
units.proposition: The supervisory authority competent pursuant to Article 56(1) or (4) shall invite the supervisory authority of each concerned Member State to take part in the joint operations when the conditions in Article 62(2) are met.

units.action: cooperate with each other through the consistency mechanism as set out in this Section
units.scope: to contribute to the consistent application of this Regulation throughout the Union
units.proposition: Supervisory authorities are obliged to cooperate with each other through the consistency mechanism as set out in this Section to contribute to the consistent application of this Regulation throughout the Union.

units.action: issue an opinion
units.condition: where a competent supervisory authority intends to adopt a list of the processing operations subject to the requirement for a data protection impact assessment pursuant to Article 35(4)
units.proposition: The Board is obliged to issue an opinion when a competent supervisory authority intends to adopt a list of processing operations subject to a data protection impact assessment pursuant to Article 35(4).

units.action: issue an opinion
units.condition: where a competent supervisory authority's draft decision concerns, pursuant to Article 40(7), whether a draft code of conduct or an amendment or extension to a code of conduct complies with this Regulation
units.proposition: The Board is obliged to issue an opinion when a competent supervisory authority's draft decision concerns, pursuant to Article 40(7), whether a draft code of conduct or an amendment or extension to a code of conduct complies with this Regulation.

units.action: promote cooperation and the effective bilateral and multilateral exchange of information and best practices
units.scope: between the supervisory authorities
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board shall promote cooperation and the effective bilateral and multilateral exchange of information and best practices between the supervisory authorities.

units.action: promote common training programmes
units.scope: for supervisory authorities
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board shall promote common training programmes for supervisory authorities.

units.action: facilitate personnel exchanges
units.scope: between supervisory authorities
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board shall facilitate personnel exchanges between supervisory authorities.

units.action: adopt a binding decision
units.scope: individual case under the cooperation procedure
units.condition: where, in a case referred to in Article 60(4), a supervisory authority concerned has raised a relevant and reasoned objection to a draft decision of the lead authority, or the lead authority has rejected such an objection as not relevant or not reasoned
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board is obliged to adopt a binding decision where, in a case under Article 60(4), a supervisory authority concerned has raised a relevant and reasoned objection to a draft decision of the lead authority, or the lead authority has rejected such an objection as not relevant or reasoned.

units.action: ensure its binding decision concerns all matters that are the subject of the relevant and reasoned objection, including whether there is an infringement of the Regulation
units.scope: content of the binding decision under point (a)
units.condition: in the situation referred to in paragraph 1(a)
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board is obliged, in the situation referred to in paragraph 1(a), to ensure its binding decision concerns all matters that are the subject of the relevant and reasoned objection, including whether there is an infringement of the Regulation.

units.action: adopt a binding decision
units.scope: dispute on competence for the main establishment
units.condition: where there are conflicting views on which of the supervisory authorities concerned is competent for the main establishment
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board is obliged to adopt a binding decision where there are conflicting views on which of the supervisory authorities concerned is competent for the main establishment.

units.action: adopt provisional measures intended to produce legal effects with a specified period of validity
units.scope: on its own territory
units.condition: in exceptional circumstances where it considers there is an urgent need to act to protect the rights and freedoms of data subjects
units.exception: by way of derogation from the consistency mechanism in Articles 63, 64 and 65 and the procedure in Article 60
units.proposition: A supervisory authority concerned may, in exceptional circumstances where it considers an urgent need to act to protect data subjects’ rights and freedoms, immediately adopt provisional measures producing legal effects on its own territory, by way of derogation from Articles 60 and 63–65, with a specified period of validity.

units.addressee: supervisory authority that adopted provisional measures under Article 66(1)
units.action: communicate the adopted provisional measures and the reasons for adopting them to the other supervisory authorities concerned, the Board and the Commission
units.scope: measures adopted under Article 66(1)
units.condition: after adopting provisional measures under paragraph 1
units.proposition: The supervisory authority that adopted provisional measures under Article 66(1) shall, without delay, communicate those measures and the reasons for adopting them to the other supervisory authorities concerned, to the Board and to the Commission.

units.action: specify a period of validity for the provisional measures it adopts under Article 66(1)
units.scope: provisional measures under Article 66(1)
units.condition: when adopting provisional measures under paragraph 1
units.proposition: When adopting provisional measures under Article 66(1), the supervisory authority concerned shall specify a period of validity for those measures.

units.ru_label: Commission may adopt acts for info exchange
units.action: adopt implementing acts of general scope to specify arrangements for the exchange of information by electronic means between supervisory authorities and between supervisory authorities and the European Data Protection Board, including the standardised format referred to in Article 64
units.scope: Arrangements and standardised formats for electronic information exchange between supervisory authorities and between supervisory authorities and the European Data Protection Board
units.proposition: The European Commission has the power to adopt implementing acts of general scope to specify arrangements, including the standardised format referred to in Article 64, for the electronic exchange of information between supervisory authorities and between supervisory authorities and the European Data Protection Board.

units.addressee: Chair of the European Data Protection Board
units.action: represent the European Data Protection Board
units.scope: representation of the European Data Protection Board
units.proposition: The Chair of the European Data Protection Board has the power to represent the Board.

units.addressee: Member State with more than one supervisory authority responsible under the GDPR
units.action: appoint a joint representative in accordance with its law
units.scope: representation of that Member State’s supervisory authorities on the Board
units.condition: Where in a Member State more than one supervisory authority is responsible for monitoring application of the GDPR
units.proposition: Where a Member State has more than one supervisory authority, that Member State must appoint a joint representative in accordance with its law.

units.action: participate in the activities and meetings of the European Data Protection Board
units.scope: activities and meetings of the European Data Protection Board
units.proposition: The European Commission has the right to participate in the activities and meetings of the European Data Protection Board.

units.action: act independently
units.scope: performance of tasks and exercise of powers pursuant to Articles 70 and 71
units.temporal: when performing its tasks or exercising its powers pursuant to Articles 70 and 71
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board is obliged to act independently when performing its tasks or exercising its powers pursuant to Articles 70 and 71.

units.action: seek instructions from anybody
units.scope: performance of its tasks or exercise of its powers
units.exception: Without prejudice to requests by the Commission referred to in point (b) of Article 70(1) and in Article 70(2)
units.temporal: in the performance of its tasks or the exercise of its powers
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board is prohibited from seeking instructions from anybody when performing its tasks or exercising its powers, without prejudice to requests by the Commission referred to in point (b) of Article 70(1) and in Article 70(2).

units.action: ensure the consistent application of the GDPR
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board shall ensure the consistent application of the GDPR.

units.action: monitor the correct application of the GDPR
units.scope: in the cases provided for in Articles 64 and 65
units.condition: on its own initiative or, where relevant, at the request of the European Commission
units.exception: without prejudice to the tasks of national supervisory authorities
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board shall monitor the correct application of the GDPR in the cases provided for in Articles 64 and 65, on its own initiative or, where relevant, at the request of the European Commission, without prejudice to the tasks of national supervisory authorities.

units.action: advise the European Commission on issues related to the protection of personal data in the Union
units.scope: including on any proposed amendment of the GDPR
units.condition: on its own initiative or, where relevant, at the request of the European Commission
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board shall advise the European Commission on any issue related to the protection of personal data in the Union, including on any proposed amendment of the GDPR, on its own initiative or, where relevant, at the request of the European Commission.

units.action: draw up an annual report on the protection of natural persons with regard to processing
units.scope: geographical coverage: the Union; and, for coverage of third countries and international organisations, where relevant
units.condition: where relevant (for coverage of third countries and international organisations)
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board is obliged to draw up an annual report on the protection of natural persons with regard to processing in the Union and, where relevant, in third countries and international organisations.

units.action: make the annual report public
units.scope: the annual report referred to in Article 71(1)
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board is obliged to make the annual report public.

units.ru_label: Board transmit annual report to EU institutions
units.action: transmit the annual report to the European Parliament, the Council and the Commission
units.scope: the annual report referred to in Article 71(1)
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board is obliged to transmit the annual report to the European Parliament, the Council and the Commission.

units.action: take decisions by a simple majority of its members
units.exception: unless otherwise provided for in this Regulation
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board is obliged to take decisions by a simple majority of its members, unless otherwise provided for in this Regulation.

units.ru_label: Adopt rules of procedure by two-thirds majority
units.action: adopt its own rules of procedure by a two-thirds majority of its members
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board is obliged to adopt its own rules of procedure by a two-thirds majority of its members.

units.action: organise its own operational arrangements
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board is obliged to organise its own operational arrangements.

units.action: elect a chair
units.scope: from amongst its members; by simple majority
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board shall elect a chair from amongst its members by simple majority.

units.action: elect two deputy chairs
units.scope: from amongst its members; by simple majority
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board shall elect two deputy chairs from amongst its members by simple majority.

units.ru_label: Chair and deputies serve five-year term
units.addressee: Chair and deputy chairs of the EDPB
units.action: serve a term of office
units.proposition: The term of office of the Chair and of the deputy chairs shall be five years.

units.action: convene the meetings of the Board
units.proposition: The Chair of the Board is obligated to convene the meetings of the Board.

units.action: prepare the agenda of the Board's meetings
units.proposition: The Chair of the Board is obligated to prepare the agenda of the Board's meetings.

units.action: notify decisions to the lead supervisory authority and the supervisory authorities concerned
units.scope: decisions adopted by the Board pursuant to Article 65
units.proposition: The Chair of the Board is obligated to notify decisions adopted by the Board pursuant to Article 65 to the lead supervisory authority and the supervisory authorities concerned.

units.action: have a secretariat
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board is obliged to have a secretariat.

units.ru_label: Secretariat acts only under Chair’s instructions
units.action: perform its tasks
units.scope: exclusively under the instructions of the Chair of the Board
units.proposition: The Board secretariat is obliged to perform its tasks exclusively under the instructions of the Chair of the Board.

units.ru_label: EDPS staff (Board tasks) have separate reporting lines
units.addressee: Staff of the European Data Protection Supervisor involved in Board tasks
units.action: be subject to separate reporting lines
units.scope: separate from staff involved in carrying out tasks conferred on the European Data Protection Supervisor
units.condition: when involved in carrying out tasks conferred on the Board by this Regulation
units.proposition: Staff of the European Data Protection Supervisor who are involved in carrying out the tasks conferred on the Board by this Regulation are obliged to be subject to separate reporting lines from staff involved in carrying out tasks conferred on the European Data Protection Supervisor.

units.action: keep its discussions confidential
units.scope: discussions of the Board
units.condition: where the Board deems it necessary, as provided for in its rules of procedure
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board is obliged to keep its discussions confidential where it deems this necessary in accordance with its rules of procedure.

units.action: apply Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001 to govern access to documents
units.scope: access to documents submitted to members of the Board, experts and representatives of third parties
units.proposition: The European Data Protection Board is obliged to apply Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001 to govern access to documents submitted to members of the Board, experts and representatives of third parties.

units.action: lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority
units.scope: in particular with a supervisory authority in the Member State of the data subject's habitual residence, place of work, or place of the alleged infringement
units.condition: if the data subject considers that the processing of personal data relating to him or her infringes this Regulation
units.proposition: Every data subject has the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority, in particular in the Member State of his or her habitual residence, place of work, or the place of the alleged infringement, if the data subject considers that the processing of personal data relating to him or her infringes this Regulation.

units.addressee: the supervisory authority with which the complaint has been lodged
units.action: inform the complainant of the possibility of a judicial remedy pursuant to Article 78
units.condition: if a complaint has been lodged with the supervisory authority
units.proposition: The supervisory authority with which the complaint has been lodged shall inform the complainant of the possibility of a judicial remedy pursuant to Article 78.

units.action: obtain an effective judicial remedy before a court
units.scope: against a legally binding decision of a supervisory authority concerning the person
units.exception: Without prejudice to any other administrative or non-judicial remedy
units.proposition: Each natural or legal person has the right to obtain an effective judicial remedy before a court against a legally binding decision of a supervisory authority concerning them.

units.action: obtain an effective judicial remedy before a court
units.scope: regarding a complaint lodged under Article 77
units.condition: where the supervisory authority competent under Articles 55 and 56 does not handle the complaint or does not inform the data subject on its progress or outcome within three months
units.exception: Without prejudice to any other administrative or non-judicial remedy
units.proposition: Each data subject has the right to obtain an effective judicial remedy before a court regarding a complaint lodged under Article 77 where the supervisory authority competent under Articles 55 and 56 does not handle the complaint or does not inform the data subject on its progress or outcome within three months.

units.addressee: any person bringing proceedings against a supervisory authority
units.action: bring the proceedings before the courts of the Member State where the supervisory authority is established
units.scope: proceedings against a supervisory authority
units.proposition: Any person bringing proceedings against a supervisory authority must bring the proceedings before the courts of the Member State where that supervisory authority is established.

units.action: seek an effective judicial remedy before a court against a controller or processor
units.scope: in addition to any available administrative or non-judicial remedies, including the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority under Article 77
units.condition: the data subject considers that his or her rights under the GDPR have been infringed as a result of processing of his or her personal data in non-compliance with the GDPR
units.proposition: Each data subject has the right to seek an effective judicial remedy against a controller or processor when they consider that their GDPR rights have been infringed due to non-compliant processing of their personal data, in addition to any available administrative or non-judicial remedies including the right to lodge a complaint under Article 77.

units.action: bring proceedings against a controller or processor before the courts of the Member State where the controller or processor has an establishment
units.scope: judicial proceedings under Article 79
units.proposition: A data subject has the power to bring proceedings against a controller or processor before the courts of the Member State where the controller or processor has an establishment.

units.ru_label: Forum option: habitual residence (not public authority)
units.action: bring proceedings against a controller or processor before the courts of the Member State where the data subject has his or her habitual residence
units.scope: judicial proceedings under Article 79
units.exception: unless the controller or processor is a public authority of a Member State acting in the exercise of its public powers
units.proposition: A data subject has the power to bring proceedings under Article 79 before the courts of the Member State of their habitual residence, unless the controller or processor is a public authority of a Member State acting in the exercise of its public powers.

units.ru_label: DS may mandate body to lodge complaint
units.action: mandate a qualified not-for-profit body, organisation or association to lodge the complaint on the data subject's behalf
units.scope: The representative must be not-for-profit, properly constituted under the law of a Member State, have statutory objectives in the public interest, and be active in protecting data subjects' rights and freedoms regarding personal data
units.proposition: The data subject has the right to mandate a qualified not-for-profit body to lodge the complaint on his or her behalf.

units.ru_label: DS may mandate body to exercise Art77 right
units.action: mandate a qualified not-for-profit body, organisation or association to exercise the right referred to in Article 77 on the data subject's behalf
units.scope: The representative must be not-for-profit, properly constituted under the law of a Member State, have statutory objectives in the public interest, and be active in protecting data subjects' rights and freedoms regarding personal data
units.proposition: The data subject has the right to mandate a qualified not-for-profit body to exercise the right referred to in Article 77 on his or her behalf.

units.ru_label: DS may mandate body to claim Art82 compensation if provided by MS law
units.action: mandate a qualified not-for-profit body, organisation or association to exercise the right to receive compensation referred to in Article 82 on the data subject's behalf
units.scope: The representative must be not-for-profit, properly constituted under the law of a Member State, have statutory objectives in the public interest, and be active in protecting data subjects' rights and freedoms regarding personal data
units.condition: Where provided for by Member State law
units.proposition: The data subject has the right to mandate a qualified not-for-profit body to exercise on his or her behalf the right to receive compensation referred to in Article 82 where provided for by Member State law.

units.addressee: a competent court of a Member State
units.action: contact the court in the other Member State to confirm the existence of the parallel proceedings
units.scope: proceedings concerning the same subject matter as regards processing by the same controller or processor
units.condition: the court has information that such proceedings are pending in a court in another Member State
units.proposition: A competent court of a Member State must contact the court in another Member State to confirm the existence of parallel proceedings when it has information that proceedings concerning the same subject matter as regards processing by the same controller or processor are pending there.

units.addressee: any competent court other than the court first seized
units.action: suspend its proceedings
units.scope: proceedings concerning the same subject matter as regards processing by the same controller or processor
units.condition: such proceedings are pending in a court in another Member State
units.proposition: Any competent court other than the court first seized may suspend its proceedings when proceedings concerning the same subject matter as regards processing by the same controller or processor are pending in a court in another Member State.

units.addressee: any court other than the court first seized
units.action: decline jurisdiction
units.scope: actions in question relating to the same subject matter of processing by the same controller or processor
units.condition: a party applies; the court first seized has jurisdiction over the actions in question; and the law of the court first seized permits consolidation of those actions
units.temporal: when the proceedings in the other Member State are pending at first instance
units.proposition: Any court other than the court first seized may, on application of a party, decline jurisdiction when the proceedings in the other Member State are pending at first instance, the court first seized has jurisdiction over the actions in question, and its law permits consolidation.

units.addressee: any person who has suffered material or non-material damage
units.action: receive compensation from the controller or processor for the damage suffered
units.scope: damage resulting from an infringement of this Regulation
units.condition: the person has suffered material or non-material damage as a result of an infringement of this Regulation
units.proposition: Any person who has suffered material or non-material damage as a result of an infringement of this Regulation has the right to receive compensation from the controller or processor for the damage suffered.

units.action: be liable for the damage caused by processing that infringes this Regulation
units.scope: damage caused by processing
units.condition: the processing infringes this Regulation
units.proposition: Any controller involved in processing shall be liable for damage caused by processing that infringes this Regulation.

units.action: be liable for the damage caused by processing
units.scope: processor liability for damage caused by processing
units.condition: the processor has not complied with obligations of this Regulation specifically directed to processors or has acted outside or contrary to the controller’s lawful instructions
units.proposition: A processor shall be liable for damage caused by processing only where it has not complied with obligations of this Regulation specifically directed to processors or has acted outside or contrary to the controller’s lawful instructions.

units.ru_label: Ensure fines are effective, proportionate, dissuasive
units.action: ensure that the imposition of administrative fines is effective, proportionate and dissuasive
units.scope: administrative fines imposed pursuant to Article 83 for infringements referred to in paragraphs 4, 5 and 6
units.condition: in each individual case
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority shall ensure that the imposition of administrative fines pursuant to Article 83 for infringements referred to in paragraphs 4, 5 and 6 is, in each individual case, effective, proportionate and dissuasive.

units.ru_label: Power to cumulate or substitute fines with 58(2) measures
units.action: impose an administrative fine in addition to, or instead of, measures under Article 58(2)(a)–(h) and (j)
units.scope: enforcement measures under Article 58(2)
units.condition: depending on the circumstances of each individual case
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority has the power, depending on the circumstances of each individual case, to impose an administrative fine in addition to, or instead of, measures under Article 58(2)(a)–(h) and (j).

units.ru_label: Due regard: nature, gravity, duration (and processing context, affected subjects, damage)
units.action: give due regard to the nature, gravity and duration of the infringement
units.scope: including the nature, scope or purpose of the processing concerned, the number of data subjects affected, and the level of damage suffered by them
units.temporal: when deciding whether to impose an administrative fine and when deciding on the amount in each individual case
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority shall, when deciding whether to impose an administrative fine and on the amount in each individual case, give due regard to the nature, gravity and duration of the infringement, including the nature, scope or purpose of the processing concerned, the number of data subjects affected, and the level of damage suffered by them.

units.action: lay down rules on other penalties applicable to infringements of this Regulation
units.scope: particularly for infringements not subject to administrative fines under Article 83
units.proposition: Member States shall lay down rules on other penalties applicable to infringements of the GDPR, particularly where infringements are not subject to administrative fines under Article 83.

units.action: take all measures necessary to ensure that the penalties laid down under Article 84(1) are implemented
units.proposition: Member States shall take all measures necessary to ensure that the penalties laid down under Article 84(1) are implemented.

units.action: ensure that penalties laid down under Article 84(1) are effective, proportionate and dissuasive
units.proposition: Member States shall ensure that penalties laid down under Article 84(1) are effective, proportionate and dissuasive.

units.action: reconcile by law the right to the protection of personal data under this Regulation with the right to freedom of expression and information
units.scope: including processing for journalistic purposes and for academic, artistic or literary expression
units.proposition: Member States must, by law, reconcile the right to the protection of personal data under this Regulation with the right to freedom of expression and information, including for processing for journalistic, academic, artistic or literary purposes.

units.action: provide for exemptions or derogations from Chapters II, III, IV, V, VI, VII and IX of the GDPR
units.scope: processing carried out for journalistic purposes or for academic, artistic or literary expression
units.condition: if necessary to reconcile the right to the protection of personal data with the freedom of expression and information
units.proposition: For processing carried out for journalistic or for academic, artistic or literary expression, Member States must provide for exemptions or derogations from Chapters II, III, IV, V, VI, VII and IX where necessary to reconcile data protection with freedom of expression and information.

units.action: notify the Commission of the provisions of its law adopted pursuant to paragraph 2
units.proposition: Each Member State must notify the Commission of the provisions of its law adopted pursuant to Article 85(2).

units.ru_label: Disclosure of personal data in official documents
units.addressee: public authorities, public bodies, and private bodies performing a task carried out in the public interest that hold official documents
units.action: disclose personal data contained in official documents they hold
units.scope: personal data in official documents held for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest
units.condition: the disclosure is made in accordance with Union or Member State law to which the public authority or body is subject and aims to reconcile public access to official documents with the right to the protection of personal data pursuant to the GDPR
units.proposition: A public authority, public body, or private body performing a task in the public interest that holds official documents may disclose personal data contained in those documents in accordance with applicable Union or Member State law, to reconcile public access to official documents with the right to the protection of personal data.

units.action: determine specific conditions for the processing of national identification numbers or other identifiers of general application
units.scope: processing of national identification numbers or other identifiers of general application
units.proposition: Member States have the power to further determine specific conditions for processing national identification numbers or other identifiers of general application.

units.action: use national identification numbers or other identifiers of general application only under appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of the data subject
units.scope: use/processing of national identification numbers or other identifiers of general application pursuant to the GDPR
units.condition: where a Member State has determined specific conditions for processing such identifiers
units.proposition: Where a Member State has determined specific conditions for processing such identifiers, controllers shall use national identification numbers or other identifiers of general application only under appropriate safeguards for the data subject’s rights and freedoms pursuant to the GDPR.

units.action: provide more specific rules by law or by collective agreements
units.scope: to ensure the protection of rights and freedoms in respect of the processing of employees' personal data in the employment context, particularly for recruitment; performance of the contract of employment (including discharge of legal or collectively agreed obligations); management, planning and organisation of work; equality and diversity in the workplace; health and safety at work; protection of employer's or customer's property; exercise and enjoyment of employment-related rights and benefits; and termination of the employment relationship
units.proposition: Member States may, by law or by collective agreements, provide for more specific rules to ensure the protection of rights and freedoms in respect of the processing of employees' personal data in the employment context for the listed employment-related purposes.

units.addressee: Member States and social partners concluding collective agreements under Article 88(1)
units.action: include suitable and specific measures to safeguard data subjects' human dignity, legitimate interests and fundamental rights in those rules
units.scope: with particular regard to transparency of processing, transfers of personal data within a group of undertakings or a group of enterprises engaged in a joint economic activity, and monitoring systems at the workplace
units.condition: when adopting rules under Article 88(1)
units.proposition: When adopting rules under Article 88(1), Member States and social partners concluding collective agreements shall include suitable and specific measures to safeguard the data subject's human dignity, legitimate interests and fundamental rights, with particular regard to transparency of processing, intra‑group transfers of personal data, and monitoring systems at the workplace.

units.action: notify to the Commission the provisions of its law adopted pursuant to Article 88(1)
units.proposition: Each Member State shall notify to the Commission, by 25 May 2018, the provisions of its law adopted pursuant to Article 88(1).

units.action: subject processing to appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of the data subject
units.scope: appropriate safeguards in accordance with the GDPR
units.condition: when processing personal data for archiving in the public interest, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes
units.proposition: Controllers must, when processing personal data for archiving in the public interest, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes, subject the processing to appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of the data subject in accordance with the GDPR.

units.action: ensure technical and organisational measures are in place to respect the principle of data minimisation
units.scope: safeguards for processing under Article 89(1)
units.condition: when applying safeguards for processing for archiving in the public interest, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes
units.proposition: Controllers must, when applying safeguards for processing for archiving in the public interest, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes, ensure technical and organisational measures are in place to respect the principle of data minimisation.

units.action: include pseudonymisation among the technical and organisational measures
units.scope: measures implemented under the safeguards to ensure data minimisation
units.condition: provided that the archiving in the public interest, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes can be fulfilled in that manner
units.proposition: Controllers may include pseudonymisation among the technical and organisational measures, provided that the archiving in the public interest, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes can be fulfilled in that manner.

units.ru_label: MS may adopt secrecy-specific SA power rules
units.action: adopt specific rules to set out the powers of the supervisory authorities laid down in points (e) and (f) of Article 58(1) in relation to certain controllers or processors
units.scope: controllers or processors that are subject to an obligation of professional secrecy or equivalent obligations of secrecy under Union or Member State law or rules established by national competent bodies
units.condition: where necessary and proportionate to reconcile the right to the protection of personal data with the obligation of secrecy
units.proposition: Member States may adopt specific rules setting out the supervisory authorities’ powers under Article 58(1)(e) and (f) in relation to controllers or processors subject to professional or equivalent secrecy obligations, where this is necessary and proportionate to reconcile data protection with secrecy.

units.ru_label: Limit application of adopted rules to secrecy‑obtained data
units.action: apply rules adopted under Article 90(1) to personal data other than data received or obtained in an activity covered by the secrecy obligation
units.scope: rules adopted pursuant to Article 90(1)
units.proposition: Member States shall not apply the rules adopted under Article 90(1) to personal data other than personal data that a controller or processor received or obtained in an activity covered by the secrecy obligation.

units.ru_label: Notify adopted rules to Commission by 25 May 2018
units.action: notify to the Commission the rules adopted pursuant to Article 90(1)
units.condition: upon adoption of rules pursuant to Article 90(1)
units.proposition: Each Member State shall notify to the Commission the rules adopted pursuant to Article 90(1) by 25 May 2018.

units.ru_label: Existing church rules may continue if aligned
units.addressee: churches and religious associations or communities
units.action: continue to apply their pre-existing comprehensive data-protection rules
units.scope: in a Member State
units.condition: the entities applied such comprehensive rules at the time of entry into force of this Regulation and the rules are brought into line with this Regulation
units.proposition: Churches and religious associations or communities may continue to apply their pre-existing comprehensive data-protection rules in a Member State if those rules were in force at the time of entry into force of this Regulation and are brought into line with this Regulation.

units.action: be subject to the supervision of an independent supervisory authority
units.condition: they apply comprehensive rules in accordance with Article 91(1)
units.proposition: Churches and religious associations must be subject to the supervision of an independent supervisory authority when they apply comprehensive rules in accordance with Article 91(1).

units.action: designate a specific independent supervisory authority for supervising churches and religious associations that apply comprehensive rules under Article 91(1)
units.condition: the designated specific authority fulfils the conditions laid down in Chapter VI of this Regulation
units.proposition: Member States may designate a specific independent supervisory authority to supervise churches and religious associations that apply comprehensive rules under Article 91(1), provided that the authority fulfils the conditions laid down in Chapter VI of this Regulation.

units.action: adopt delegated acts
units.condition: subject to the conditions laid down in Article 92
units.proposition: The European Commission has the power to adopt delegated acts subject to the conditions laid down in Article 92.

units.action: exercise the delegated power referred to in Article 12(8) and Article 43(8)
units.scope: for an indeterminate period of time
units.proposition: The European Commission has the delegated power referred to in Article 12(8) and Article 43(8) for an indeterminate period starting on 24 May 2016.

units.action: revoke the delegation of power referred to in Article 12(8) and Article 43(8)
units.exception: Revocation shall not affect the validity of any delegated acts already in force.
units.consequence: A revocation decision ends the delegation of power specified in the decision and takes effect the day after its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union or on a later date specified in the decision.
units.proposition: The European Parliament has the power to revoke at any time the delegation of power referred to in Article 12(8) and Article 43(8), with the revocation decision ending the specified delegation and taking effect the day after its publication or on a later specified date, without affecting the validity of any delegated acts already in force.

units.action: be assisted by a committee
units.proposition: The European Commission is obliged to be assisted by a committee.

units.action: ensure that the assisting committee is a committee within the meaning of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011
units.condition: for the committee referred to in paragraph 1
units.proposition: The European Commission is obliged to ensure that the assisting committee is a committee within the meaning of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011.

units.action: apply Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011
units.condition: where reference is made to paragraph 2 of this Article
units.proposition: When reference is made to paragraph 2 of this Article, Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011 must be applied.

units.ru_label: Construe references to repealed Directive as this Regulation
units.action: construe references to Directive 95/46/EC as references to this Regulation
units.condition: when interpreting or applying texts that contain references to the repealed Directive 95/46/EC
units.proposition: References to Directive 95/46/EC must be construed as references to this Regulation.

units.ru_label: Construe references to Article 29 Working Party as EDPB
units.action: construe references to the Working Party on the Protection of Individuals with regard to the Processing of Personal Data established by Article 29 of Directive 95/46/EC as references to the European Data Protection Board established by this Regulation
units.condition: when interpreting or applying texts that contain references to the Article 29 Working Party
units.proposition: References to the Article 29 Working Party must be construed as references to the European Data Protection Board.

units.ru_label: No additional GDPR obligations where ePrivacy applies
units.action: impose additional obligations on natural or legal persons
units.scope: in relation to processing in connection with the provision of publicly available electronic communications services in public communication networks in the Union
units.condition: for matters for which those persons are subject to specific obligations with the same objective under Directive 2002/58/EC
units.proposition: This Regulation is prohibited from imposing additional obligations on natural or legal persons regarding processing connected to the provision of publicly available electronic communications services in public communication networks in the Union where those persons are already subject to specific obligations with the same objective under Directive 2002/58/EC.

units.ru_label: Previously concluded data-transfer agreements remain in force
units.action: recognise the continued validity of specified international agreements
units.scope: international agreements involving the transfer of personal data to third countries or international organisations
units.condition: the agreement was concluded by a Member State prior to 24 May 2016 and complied with Union law applicable prior to that date
units.temporal: until the agreement is amended, replaced or revoked
units.proposition: Member States shall recognise the continued validity of international agreements involving transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations that were concluded before 24 May 2016 and complied with Union law applicable at that time, until those agreements are amended, replaced or revoked.

units.action: make the reports public
units.scope: reports on the evaluation and review of this Regulation
units.proposition: The European Commission shall make the reports on the evaluation and review of this Regulation public.

units.action: examine the application and functioning of Chapter V on the transfer of personal data to third countries or international organisations
units.scope: with particular regard to decisions adopted pursuant to Article 45(3) GDPR and decisions adopted on the basis of Article 25(6) of Directive 95/46/EC
units.condition: in the context of the evaluations and reviews referred to in paragraph 1
units.proposition: In the context of the evaluations and reviews referred to in paragraph 1, the European Commission shall examine the application and functioning of Chapter V on the transfer of personal data to third countries or international organisations, with particular regard to decisions adopted pursuant to Article 45(3) GDPR and decisions adopted on the basis of Article 25(6) of Directive 95/46/EC.

units.action: examine the application and functioning of Chapter VII on cooperation and consistency
units.condition: in the context of the evaluations and reviews referred to in paragraph 1
units.proposition: In the context of the evaluations and reviews referred to in paragraph 1, the European Commission shall examine the application and functioning of Chapter VII on cooperation and consistency.

units.ru_label: Commission to propose amendments to other data-protection acts
units.action: submit legislative proposals with a view to amending other Union legal acts on the protection of personal data
units.scope: to ensure uniform and consistent protection of natural persons with regard to processing; in particular concerning rules on processing by Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies, and on the free movement of such data
units.condition: if appropriate
units.proposition: The Commission is obligated, if appropriate, to submit legislative proposals to amend other Union legal acts on the protection of personal data in order to ensure uniform and consistent protection of natural persons with regard to processing, in particular concerning rules on processing by Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies and on the free movement of such data.

units.action: treat the Regulation as binding in its entirety
units.scope: in all Member States
units.proposition: Member States must treat the Regulation as binding in its entirety.

units.action: apply the Regulation directly without requiring national transposition measures
units.scope: in all Member States
units.proposition: Member States must apply the Regulation directly without requiring national transposition measures.

units.addressee: court seized of proceedings against a decision by a supervisory authority
units.action: contact the competent court in another Member State to confirm the existence of related proceedings
units.scope: proceedings against a decision by a supervisory authority
units.condition: the seized court has reason to believe that proceedings concerning the same processing are brought before a competent court in another Member State
units.proposition: A court seized of proceedings against a decision by a supervisory authority is obliged to contact the competent court in another Member State to confirm the existence of related proceedings when it has reason to believe that proceedings concerning the same processing are brought there.

units.addressee: any court other than the court first seized
units.action: stay its proceedings
units.condition: related proceedings are pending before a court in another Member State
units.proposition: Any court other than the court first seized is permitted to stay its proceedings when related proceedings are pending before a court in another Member State.

units.action: treat proceedings as related
units.condition: the proceedings are so closely connected that it is expedient to hear and determine them together to avoid the risk of irreconcilable judgments from separate proceedings
units.proposition: Courts are obliged to treat proceedings as related where they are so closely connected that it is expedient to hear and determine them together to avoid the risk of irreconcilable judgments from separate proceedings.

units.ru_label: No referral at request of time-barred person
units.action: refer a question on the validity of a Board decision to the Court of Justice at the request of a natural or legal person
units.scope: validity of a decision of the European Data Protection Board
units.condition: the requesting natural or legal person had the opportunity to bring an action for annulment of that decision, in particular because it was directly and individually concerned, but did not bring such an action
units.temporal: within the period laid down in Article 263 TFEU
units.proposition: A national court is prohibited from referring a question on the validity of an EDPB decision to the Court of Justice at the request of a natural or legal person that could have brought an annulment action, in particular if directly and individually concerned, but did not do so within the time limit laid down in Article 263 TFEU.
